claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's lovely to help you with your enquiry about Alex.

I have a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

Is Alex living with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Could you tell me a bit more about Alex's current living situation? For example:

- Is he living with another family member or someone else?
- Is he in local authority care?
- Is he in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's actually been in hospital for a while now - about three months or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital. I hope he's getting the care he needs.

To help me understand your situation better, could you tell me:

Was Alex living with you before he went into hospital three months ago?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he was living with me before he went into hospital.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

One more question about Alex's hospital stay: Are you contributing towards the cost of his accommodation or meals while he's in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I still buy things for him - clothes, magazines, his favorite snacks and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's good to hear you're still supporting Alex with his needs.

I just have a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one final question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 6 years old
- He was living with you before going into hospital
- He has been in hospital for around 3 months (approximately 12 weeks)
- You are regularly spending money on him (clothes, snacks, magazines, etc.)
- You live in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- **Alex is under 16** and you live in the UK, which meets the basic eligibility criteria.
- Although Alex has been in hospital for around 12 weeks (which is normally the point at which Child Benefit might be affected), **there is an exception** that applies to your situation.
- Because Alex is in a **UK hospital** and you are **regularly spending money on him** (buying clothes, snacks, magazines, etc.), you can continue to receive Child Benefit.

**Important:** You should inform HMRC about Alex's hospital stay if you haven't already done so. You can do this by filling in an online form or by contacting them by phone or post. This ensures your claim is properly recorded and you continue to receive your payments without any issues.

I hope Alex gets well soon. If you have any other questions, please don't hesitate to ask.

The claimant has confirmed they are regularly contributing towards Alex's needs by buying him clothes, magazines, and snacks. Since Alex was living with the claimant before hospitalisation, the claimant is in the UK and regularly spending money on Alex, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, the claimant meets the eligibility criteria under this exception.
